---
title: Answer a question or a refusal
---

Sentinel answers each action in one of three ways: approved, prompt, or deny.
Most actions proceed with no message.
An action that is legitimate but risky, such as `git reset --hard`, makes Sentinel ask you.
An action that no project work needs, such as reading an SSH private key, is refused.

## When Sentinel prompts

The agent stops and prompts you before the action runs.
The prompt includes the command or file and says what approving it permits.

| Agent                     | What you see                                                                                       |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code               | a permission prompt with Sentinel's reason                                                         |
| GitHub Copilot CLI        | a permission prompt with Sentinel's reason, in an interactive session                              |
| GitHub Copilot in VS Code | a confirmation in the chat with Sentinel's reason                                                  |
| Pi                        | a confirmation titled "A hook asks before *tool* runs", with Sentinel's reason                     |
| Codex                     | no prompt: Codex cannot show one, so Sentinel refuses the action                                 |

Copilot CLI cannot show a prompt in a session started with `-p` or in autopilot mode; in these cases, Copilot CLI refuses the action instead.
In assisted mode, a model can answer Sentinel's question instead of you.
The [session-start report](session-start-report.qmd) warns when your settings can select assisted mode.

If a prompt is declined, the action does not run, and the agent is told that you declined.

## When Sentinel refuses

The action does not run.
The agent receives Sentinel's message, which starts with `Blocked:` and explains what was refused, why, and what to do next:

- In most cases, the agent is told to stop and to give you what you need to decide whether to run the action yourself.
- If the agent can do the same work with a command Sentinel accepts, the message lists those commands.
- If the agent named a relative path that Sentinel cannot resolve, the agent is told to name every path in full.

### If you need the action

Run the command in your own terminal; this is annoying but maintains the security posture.

### If the refusal is wrong (false positive)

Run the action yourself, then report the refusal at <https://github.com/ahgraber/sentinel-hooks/issues>.
Include the command or file and Sentinel's message.

## When Sentinel refuses every action

Two conditions make Sentinel refuse every action an agent takes:

**A damaged install.**
Sentinel refuses every action when it cannot read its own list of tools.
Try reinstalling Sentinel.

**Codex after an update.**
A Codex update may remove or disable a Sentinel hook file.
The error message starts with `Sentinel:` and should indicate which hook file is missing.
Run the command in the message, which runs the hook installer again.
